165# Document statuses the pipeline resumes AUTOMATICALLY — the initial snapshot 

166# of every run and every quiescence refetch, AND the only statuses any 

167# ``_next_scheduling_page`` sweep ever carries. PROCESSING/PARSING/ANALYZING 

168# are dead-process orphans (an interrupted run left them mid-flight) and must 

169# self-heal; FAILED is deliberately absent: a document that genuinely failed is 

170# retried only through an explicit manual request, whose EXCLUSIVE_RESET phase 

171# pages FAILED→PENDING via ``_next_failed_page`` with no worker running (LR2 

172# §7.3) — never as a side effect of an unrelated upload or rescan. 

173_AUTO_RESUME_DOC_STATUSES = ( 

174 DocStatus.PENDING, 

175 DocStatus.PROCESSING, 

176 DocStatus.PARSING, 

177 DocStatus.ANALYZING, 

178) 

179 

180# Multiprocess feeder poll interval: the Manager-backed ingress has no async 

181# ``get_document``, so the feeder blocks a worker thread in 

182# ``wait_for_documents(timeout)`` and re-checks between polls. Bounded by the 

183# mailbox's own MAX_MAILBOX_WAIT_SECONDS clamp; the single-process feeder is 

184# fully event-driven (``await get_document()``) and never polls. 

185_FEEDER_POLL_SECONDS = 0.5 

186 

187# Max documents the feeder drains (and admits) per iteration before returning 

188# to its top-of-loop control check. Bounds the destructive-drain re-publish 

189# burst on a teardown; cancellation and a pending manual request are ALSO 

190# re-checked before every single admission, so the per-signal yield latency is 

191# one admission, not a whole drain. 

192_FEEDER_DRAIN_LIMIT = 256 

193 

194# Manual DRAIN_TO_IDLE poll: how long to sleep between re-checks while waiting 

195# for pre-freeze in-flight enqueue reservations (pending_enqueues > 0) to 

196# finish (LR2 §7.2 step 5). Bounded by the background enqueue's own duration — 

197# the freeze admits no NEW reservations, so the count only decreases — and, when 

198# it does not decrease at all, by _MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS below. 

199_MANUAL_DRAIN_POLL_SECONDS = 0.2 

200 

201# How many ``_MANUAL_DRAIN_POLL_SECONDS`` re-checks a SCAN-driven reset gives the 

202# in-flight enqueue count before abandoning the reset (LR2 §8.1). Far shorter 

203# than the manual endpoint's own drain wait, because a scan was only granted its 

204# reservation while ``pending_enqueues == 0``, so a non-zero count here means a 

205# reservation slipped into the window before the freeze went up: wait it out 

206# briefly, then leave the request to the standard drain path rather than blocking 

207# file discovery behind it. 

208_SCAN_DRAIN_CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS = 25 

209 

210# How many consecutive DRAIN_TO_IDLE confirmation rounds may report the SAME 

211# blocking active rows before the drain is declared stalled and the workspace is 

212# fenced (LR2 §7.2 "DRAIN_TO_IDLE 的前进性" / §13.2 case 16). 

213# 

214# One round is not evidence: the confirmation sweep legitimately returns rows the 

215# run then processes. But a round that changes nothing produces an identical id 

216# set, and re-sweeping identical rows can only produce the same result again — so 

217# a small count separates "still draining" from "cannot drain", with no wall-clock 

218# timeout to tune. Every routed page leaves the AUTO set (terminal or FAILED), and 

219# a shrinking/changing set resets the counter, so a large-but-finite backlog is 

220# never mistaken for a stall. 

221_MANUAL_DRAIN_STALL_ROUNDS = 3 

222 

223# Upper bound on the blocking doc ids reported with the stall fence. The point is 

224# to name the offending rows, not to serialise a backlog into an error message. 

225_MANUAL_DRAIN_STALL_SAMPLE = 8 

226 

227# Same bound for the drain's blocker report (active rows the drain cannot advance 

228# at all — see ``_confirm_auto_drained``). Kept separate from the stall sample so 

229# either report can be widened without silently widening the other. 

230_MANUAL_DRAIN_BLOCKER_SAMPLE = 8 

231 

232# How long DRAIN_TO_IDLE may wait on an in-flight enqueue set that never changes 

233# before the workspace is fenced (``_fence_stalled_enqueue_drain``). 

234# 

235# Unlike the AUTO stall above, "the set did not change" cannot on its own prove a 

236# wedge: a reservation is held from admission until the enqueue's last write, and 

237# a large upload over a slow link legitimately keeps its token for minutes with 

238# nothing to report in between. There is no progress signal inside that span, so 

239# this bound is wall-clock and deliberately generous — it fires only when NOT ONE 

240# of the in-flight enqueues finished for the whole window, which a healthy 

241# producer does not reach even on a slow link. 

242# 

243# It replaces an UNBOUNDED wait, and that is the whole trade: a false positive 

244# fences the workspace (503 on every mutation) but names its own remedy and is 

245# cleared by ONE ``POST /documents/recovery/force_reset``, whereas the previous 

246# unbounded wait left ``busy`` latched with no fence for ``force_reset`` to clear 

247# and no way out short of restarting the process. Loud and recoverable beats 

248# silent and permanent; the bound is sized so that reaching it means something is 

249# genuinely stuck. 

250# 

251# What a false positive costs the slow-but-healthy producer depends on who moves 

252# first. The fence itself costs it nothing: a registered token is exempt from 

253# THIS fence kind (``_stall_fence_exempts_reserved_token``), so a producer that 

254# comes back still lands its rows as PENDING — unprocessable until an operator 

255# clears the fence, but not lost. The loss window is the operator's remedy: 

256# ``force_reset`` DROPS the in-flight reservation set for this kind (it is the 

257# blocker — clearing the fence alone changes nothing), and a producer that 

258# returns after that has no reservation left, so with admission enabled its 

259# re-weight is treated as a new reservation and may be refused after the client 

260# already got 200. An ``/upload`` is recovered by the next ``/documents/scan``; a 

261# ``/documents/text``/``/texts`` must be re-sent. That is the cost of a 

262# wall-clock bound sized for a producer that is stuck, applied to one that was 

263# only slow. 

264_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS = 600.0 

265_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_ROUNDS = max( 

266 1, int(_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS / _MANUAL_DRAIN_POLL_SECONDS) 

267) 

268 

269# Upper bound on the reservation tokens named in the enqueue-stall fence report. 

270_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SAMPLE = 8

273class _ManualDrainProgress: 

274 """Forward-progress tracker for one run's DRAIN_TO_IDLE (LR2 §7.2). 

275 

276 Run-scoped, not shared state: it only has to detect a spin WITHIN one 

277 processing run, because a run that exits releases the freeze and the next one 

278 re-drains from scratch. 

279 """ 

280 

281 __slots__ = ("_blocking_ids", "_repeats", "_enqueue_tokens", "_enqueue_repeats") 

282 

283 def __init__(self) -> None: 

284 self._blocking_ids: frozenset[str] | None = None 

285 self._repeats = 0 

286 self._enqueue_tokens: frozenset[str] | None = None 

287 self._enqueue_repeats = 0 

288 

289 def observe(self, doc_ids) -> bool: 

290 """Record one "the drain is not idle yet" observation. 

291 

292 Returns False once the SAME rows have blocked the drain for 

293 :data:`_MANUAL_DRAIN_STALL_ROUNDS` consecutive rounds — the caller must 

294 then fence rather than sweep again. 

295 """ 

296 ids = frozenset(doc_ids) 

297 if ids != self._blocking_ids: 

298 self._blocking_ids = ids 

299 self._repeats = 1 

300 return True 

301 self._repeats += 1 

302 return self._repeats < _MANUAL_DRAIN_STALL_ROUNDS 

303 

304 def observe_enqueue(self, tokens) -> bool: 

305 """Record one CONTINUE_DRAIN_WAIT poll over the in-flight token set. 

306 

307 Returns False once the SAME set has blocked the drain for 

308 :data:`_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_ROUNDS` consecutive polls — the caller 

309 must then fence rather than wait again. Any change resets the count: the 

310 freeze admits no new reservation, so the set can only shrink, and a 

311 shrink is a live producer finishing. 

312 

313 Tracked independently of :meth:`observe`: the two waits interleave within 

314 one drain (a doc published by a finishing enqueue puts the run back into 

315 sweeping), and folding them into one counter would let either reset the 

316 other's evidence. 

317 """ 

318 live = frozenset(tokens) 

319 if live != self._enqueue_tokens: 

320 self._enqueue_tokens = live 

321 self._enqueue_repeats = 1 

322 return True 

323 self._enqueue_repeats += 1 

324 return self._enqueue_repeats < _MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_ROUNDS 

325

327class PipelineNextStep(Enum): 

328 """Outcome of the atomic quiescence decision (see 

329 :meth:`_PipelineMixin._decide_pipeline_next_step`).""" 

330 

331 RELEASED = "released" 

332 CONTINUE_AUTO = "continue_auto" 

333 # A sticky manual retry is pending and the pipeline is IDLE: BEGIN the 

334 # manual protocol (LR2 §6.1/§7.2) — freeze new ingress, then drain the AUTO 

335 # backlog to idle. No FAILED is swept here; FAILED is reset only in the 

336 # exclusive phase below. The request stays sticky (ACKed after the reset). 

337 CONTINUE_MANUAL = "continue_manual" 

338 # Manual drain reached AUTO-empty but pre-freeze in-flight enqueue 

339 # reservations (pending_enqueues > 0) have not finished. Bounded-wait for 

340 # them so their PENDING docs join this drain cohort before the reset 

341 # (LR2 §7.2 step 5 / §7.3 pending_enqueues=0 precondition). 

342 CONTINUE_DRAIN_WAIT = "continue_drain_wait" 

343 # Manual drain reached strict idle (no AUTO, no in-flight, no mailbox): 

344 # enter EXCLUSIVE_RESET — page FAILED→PENDING with NO worker running, then 

345 # ACK the request and resume normal processing (LR2 §7.3). 

346 BEGIN_EXCLUSIVE_RESET = "begin_exclusive_reset" 

347 # Document messages still resident in the mailbox at quiescence (e.g. an 

348 # enqueue that landed after the batch's feeder stopped, or a stale 

349 # notification for a doc that has since reached a terminal state). The 

350 # refetch drains a bounded chunk and lets the strict scan decide: live 

351 # docs come back as the next batch, provably-stale messages are dropped. 

352 CONTINUE_DOCUMENT = "continue_document" 

353 # The in-progress bounded AUTO sweep has more pages (its keyset cursor is 

354 # not yet CURSOR_END). No wake-up signal is consumed: the run simply 

355 # fetches the next page of the SAME sweep before honouring quiescence 

356 # signals, so a huge PENDING backlog drains page-by-page while cancellation 

357 # and manual retry still preempt at every page boundary (LR2 Phase 2 §6.3). 

358 CONTINUE_SWEEP_PAGE = "continue_sweep_page" 

359 # Cancellation pending: the run must stop WITHOUT consuming any wake-up 

360 # signal — the ingress is fully retained for the next explicit trigger. 

361 CANCELLED = "cancelled" 

362 

363 

364@dataclass(frozen=True) 

365class PipelineNextDecision: 

366 step: PipelineNextStep 

367 # Set only for CONTINUE_MANUAL: the sticky request this continuation 

368 # serves; ACKed after the FAILED→PENDING reset persists. 

369 manual_request_id: str | None = None 

370 # Set only for CANCELLED: True when the cancellation is an internal-error 

371 # abort, whose exit path surfaces the actionable halt message. 

372 internal_error: bool = False

390class _SidecarPathOutcome(str, Enum): 

391 """Why :func:`_resolve_sidecar_image_path` did or did not return a file.""" 

392 

393 RESOLVED = "resolved" # a real file, contained to the sidecar dir 

394 REFUSED = "refused" # containment / malformed / non-string — never read 

395 MISSING = "missing" # contained but no such file on disk (or a dir) 

396 

397 

398def _resolve_sidecar_image_path( 

399 path_str: object, sidecar_dir: Path 

400) -> tuple[Path | None, _SidecarPathOutcome]: 

401 """Resolve a sidecar image reference, contained to ``sidecar_dir``. 

402 

403 The ``path`` field of ``<doc>.drawings.json`` is attacker-influenced data 

404 at rest: a sidecar can be written by an older version, by an external 

405 engine, or restored from a backup, and the value inside it originates in 

406 an uploaded document. This resolver is the sink that turns it into a file 

407 that gets read and sent to the VLM, so containment belongs here rather 

408 than resting on every producer behaving (GHSA-8rgj-chc2-6chv). 

409 

410 A legitimate value is relative and names a file inside the document's own 

411 ``<base>.blocks.assets/``. Anything that leaves ``sidecar_dir`` — an 

412 absolute path, or ``../`` — resolves outside and is refused. 

413 

414 Returns ``(path, outcome)``. The outcome lets the caller tell a genuine 

415 "no such file" (``MISSING``) apart from a containment/format refusal 

416 (``REFUSED``): a legacy sidecar whose ``path`` is an absolute 

417 RAG-Anything/MinerU value points at a file that DOES exist but sits 

418 outside the document dir, so reporting it as "not found" would send an 

419 operator debugging vanished VLM analysis away from the real cause. 

420 

421 Containment is delegated to :func:`validate_file_path_security`, the 

422 shared ``resolve()`` + ``is_relative_to()`` primitive (it folds ``..`` 

423 away, resolves both sides so a symlinked prefix like macOS 

424 ``/tmp`` → ``/private/tmp`` still matches, and converts any malformed 

425 path — embedded NUL, symlink loop — into a quiet ``None`` rather than an 

426 exception that would fail-fast the whole document). A non-string value is 

427 refused explicitly here: the shared helper would swallow the resulting 

428 ``TypeError`` via its blanket except, but the guard states the intent. 

429 """ 

430 if not isinstance(path_str, str) or not path_str: 

431 return None, _SidecarPathOutcome.REFUSED 

432 safe = validate_file_path_security(path_str, sidecar_dir) 

433 if safe is None: 

434 return None, _SidecarPathOutcome.REFUSED 

435 if safe.is_file(): 

436 return safe, _SidecarPathOutcome.RESOLVED 

437 return None, _SidecarPathOutcome.MISSING 

438

440@lru_cache(maxsize=64) 

441def _warn_content_budget_structurally_starved( 

442 *, 

443 max_extract: int, 

444 leading_cap: int, 

445 trailing_cap: int, 

446 frame_reserve: int, 

447 content_min: int, 

448) -> None: 

449 """Log once when the configured caps alone starve multimodal content. 

450 

451 ``lru_cache`` keyed on the config tuple makes this emit a single WARNING 

452 per unique configuration per process — an operator heads-up so gross 

453 misconfiguration surfaces proactively instead of as a burst of per-item 

454 :class:`MultimodalAnalysisError` failures from ``_analyze_text_modality``. 

455 

456 Conservative by design: ``frame_reserve`` counts only the fixed safety 

457 buffer, not the (item-specific, typically much larger) template frame, so 

458 ``static_room`` *overestimates* the room left for content. It therefore 

459 warns only in egregious cases where the SURROUNDING caps by themselves 

460 already leave less than ``content_min``; the per-item budget floor in 

461 ``_analyze_text_modality`` is the true enforcement. 

462 """ 

463 static_room = max_extract - leading_cap - trailing_cap - frame_reserve 

464 if static_room >= content_min: 

465 return 

466 logger.warning( 

467 "[analyze_multimodal] MAX_EXTRACT_INPUT_TOKENS=%d leaves only ~%d " 

468 "tokens for multimodal content after SURROUNDING caps (leading=%d, " 

469 "trailing=%d) and a %d-token reserve — below the content floor of %d " 

470 "(MM_EXTRACT_CONTENT_MIN_TOKENS). Items with non-trivial surrounding/" 

471 "captions will fail analysis. Raise MAX_EXTRACT_INPUT_TOKENS or lower " 

472 "SURROUNDING_LEADING_MAX_TOKENS / SURROUNDING_TRAILING_MAX_TOKENS.", 

473 max_extract, 

474 static_room, 

475 leading_cap, 

476 trailing_cap, 

477 frame_reserve, 

478 content_min, 

479 )

500 ) 

501 return resolver(source_file or file_path)

504def _rearm_auto_rescan(ingress: Any) -> None: 

505 """Set the auto-rescan dirty flag and count the re-arm (LR2 Phase 6 item 3). 

506 

507 Every re-arm costs a later strict sweep, so the rate explains sweep load that 

508 no upload accounts for. Counted here rather than inside the ingress because in 

509 multiprocess mode the mailbox lives in the Manager process, where a counter 

510 would be invisible to the worker answering /health. 

511 """ 

512 ingress.request_auto_rescan() 

513 pipeline_metrics.increment(pipeline_metrics.AUTO_RESCAN_REARMS)

549def _format_chunking_params( 

550 chunk_size: int, 

551 params: dict[str, Any], 

552) -> str: 

553 """Format the ``size=..., key=value, ...`` portion shared by the chunking 

554 start log line and ``doc_status.metadata['chunk_opts']``. 

555 

556 Drops keys with ``None``/empty values so the line stays scannable; 

557 callers pass the strategy-specific kwargs they're about to splat 

558 into the chunker so the output mirrors the actual call. Long keys are 

559 aliased to short forms via ``_CHUNK_LOG_KEY_ALIASES``. 

560 """ 

561 pieces = [f"size={chunk_size}"] 

562 for key, value in params.items(): 

563 if value is None: 

564 continue 

565 if isinstance(value, (list, dict, str)) and len(value) == 0: 565 ↛ 566line 565 didn't jump to line 566 because the condition on line 565 was never true

566 continue 

567 short = _CHUNK_LOG_KEY_ALIASES.get(key, key) 

568 pieces.append( 

569 f"{short}={value!r}" if isinstance(value, str) else f"{short}={value}" 

570 ) 

571 return ", ".join(pieces)

574@dataclass 

575class _BatchRunContext: 

576 """Per-batch shared state for the parse/analyze/process worker pipeline. 

577 

578 Bundles the cross-cutting handles (pipeline_status, locks, queues, 

579 semaphore) so worker methods accept a single ``ctx`` argument instead of 

580 ~8 individually plumbed parameters. ``processed_count`` mutates inside 

581 each batch and is always read/written under ``pipeline_status_lock``. 

582 """ 

583 

584 pipeline_status: dict 

585 pipeline_status_lock: Any 

586 semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore 

587 total_files: int 

588 # Parse queues are dynamic: one per ParserSpec.queue_group (always at 

589 # least "native"). ``parser_specs`` is the batch snapshot threaded through 

590 # routing + the parse workers so a mid-batch register_parser cannot change 

591 # the engine set for this run. 

592 parse_queues: dict[str, asyncio.Queue] 

593 parser_specs: dict 

594 q_analyze: asyncio.Queue 

595 q_process: asyncio.Queue 

596 # Process-local bridge for the shared pipeline cancellation status. Native 

597 # parser hooks run in worker threads, so they cannot await the async status 

598 # lock directly while waiting on an LLM response. 

599 pipeline_cancel_event: threading.Event | None = None 

600 processed_count: int = 0 

601 # Phase 2 in-batch feeder bookkeeping (all read/written ONLY under 

602 # ``pipeline_status_lock``): 

603 # * ``inflight_doc_ids`` — every doc_id currently routed into or moving 

604 # through the queues. The initial batch is pre-registered before the 

605 # feeder starts; the feeder adds an id right after its parse-queue put 

606 # succeeds. 

607 # * ``routing_doc_ids`` — ids being admitted right now (added before the 

608 # ``put``, moved to inflight after it with no ``await`` between the two 

609 # mutations) so the feeder's dedup sees an id the instant admission 

610 # begins — there is never a window where an admitting id is in neither 

611 # set. 

612 inflight_doc_ids: set = field(default_factory=set) 

613 routing_doc_ids: set = field(default_factory=set) 

614 # Reservation token of the run that owns ``busy`` for this batch (LR2 §7.7 

615 # items 3/4/7). Every worker status write verifies it is still the current 

616 # ``busy_owner`` before touching doc_status, so a run whose ownership was 

617 # reclaimed (dead-process reaper, Manager generation change) discards its 

618 # late results instead of writing a final status over the new owner's work. 

619 # ``None`` disables the check and exists only for call paths that construct 

620 # a context outside a reservation (tests). 

621 run_owner_token: str | None = None

623 

624class _PipelineMixin: 

625 """Mixin providing document ingestion pipeline methods for LightRAG. 

626 

627 Designed to be combined as a base of LightRAG only. Relies on 

628 LightRAG-provided attributes (``self.full_docs``, ``self.doc_status``, 

629 ``self.tokenizer``, ``self.parser_*``, ``self.workspace`` ...) and on the 

630 shared methods ``self._insert_done`` / ``self._process_extract_entities`` 

631 which remain in the main class and are resolved through MRO. 

632 """ 

633 

634 # ============================================================ 

635 # Admission control (LR2 §9) 

636 # ============================================================ 

637 

638 async def _reserve_ingress_slot( 

639 self, 

640 pipeline_status: dict[str, Any], 

641 pipeline_status_lock, 

642 *, 

643 admission_token: str | None, 

644 requested: int, 

645 reject_when, 

646 ) -> str | None: 

647 """Register this enqueue in ``pending_enqueue_tokens`` and charge 

648 ``requested`` new documents against the admission capacity (LR2 §9.2). 

649 

650 Called inside ``enqueue_serialize_lock``, after dedup and before the 

651 FIRST storage write of the critical section — the duplicate ``dup-*`` 

652 FAILED records included. That position matters three times over: 

653 

654 * the strict active count it takes cannot be raced by a sibling enqueue 

655 (which is waiting on that same lock); 

656 * ``requested`` is the real deduped count, not the coarse pre-body 

657 estimate an endpoint had to reserve with; 

658 * **the reservation is what makes the write side mutually exclusive with 

659 a manual retry.** ``manual_freeze_requested`` refuses a NEW 

660 reservation here, and DRAIN_TO_IDLE waits for ``pending_enqueues`` to 

661 reach zero (LR2 §6.1/§7.2), so the exclusive FAILED→PENDING reset 

662 cannot begin between this check and the last write below. The fence 

663 check at the top of :meth:`apipeline_enqueue_documents` cannot do 

664 that job: it takes no reservation, so it leaves the whole validate → 

665 dedup → write span invisible to the drain. 

666 

667 ``reject_when`` is passed unconditionally and 

668 :func:`acquire_enqueue_reservation` applies it only when the token is 

669 NOT already registered — i.e. only when this call mints a reservation 

670 for a reservation-less caller (SDK ``ainsert`` / direct 

671 ``apipeline_enqueue_documents``). When the caller already holds one (an 

672 endpoint reserved it, fences and all, before parsing the request body) 

673 this is a RE-WEIGHT, and a request admitted before a freeze appeared is 

674 deliberately allowed to finish — the drain is already waiting for it. 

675 Deciding that inside the reservation, from the same snapshot, is what 

676 keeps the exemption from being self-attested: passing a token string is 

677 not enough to skip a fence. A token's own previous weight is excluded 

678 from the capacity sum, so re-weighting never counts a request against 

679 itself. 

680 

681 Returns the token this function owns and the caller must release (only 

682 for a minted one), or ``None`` when the reservation belongs to the 

683 caller. 

684 

685 Raises: 

686 PipelineReservationConflictError: a mutual-exclusion fence or the 

687 recovery fence refused this reservation. Nothing has been written 

688 yet. The refusal REASON survives as data (LR2 §9.1): a caller 

689 reads ``.conflict`` / ``.recovery_required`` to tell a fenced 

690 workspace (→ 503) from a bounded manual-freeze / scan / 

691 destructive window it should retry (→ 409), rather than parsing 

692 the message. Subclasses ``RuntimeError``, so a caller written 

693 against the older coarse contract still catches it. 

694 PipelineBackpressureError: no capacity (→ 429). 

695 StorageCapabilityError / StorageControlPlaneError: the strict count 

696 failed. Deliberately propagated rather than treated as "room 

697 available" (→ 503): admission fails closed. 

698 """ 

699 from lightrag.kg.shared_storage import acquire_enqueue_reservation 

700 from lightrag.utils_pipeline import count_active_documents 

701 

702 capacity = self.max_pending_documents 

703 # Only the capacity math needs the count, and it is a strict full scan: 

704 # taking it with admission disabled would tax every enqueue for nothing. 

705 active_count = ( 

706 await count_active_documents(self.doc_status) if capacity > 0 else None 

707 ) 

708 token = admission_token or f"admission-{uuid.uuid4().hex}" 

709 result = await acquire_enqueue_reservation( 

710 pipeline_status, 

711 pipeline_status_lock, 

712 token=token, 

713 reject_when=tuple(reject_when), 

714 weight=requested, 

715 capacity=capacity, 

716 active_count=active_count, 

717 ) 

718 if not result.acquired: 

719 raise PipelineReservationConflictError( 

720 result.message or "pipeline reservation is unavailable", 

721 conflict=result.conflict, 

722 fence=result.fence, 

723 ) 

724 return None if admission_token else token 

725 

726 async def _release_admission_reservation(self, token: str) -> None: 

727 """Drop a reservation minted by :meth:`_reserve_ingress_slot`.""" 

728 from lightrag.kg.shared_storage import release_token_set_reservation 

729 

730 await release_token_set_reservation( 

731 self.workspace, 

732 tokens_key="pending_enqueue_tokens", 

733 token=token, 

734 ) 

735 

736 # ============================================================ 

737 # Public document ingestion API (entry points) 

738 # ============================================================ 

739 

740 async def apipeline_enqueue_documents( 

741 self, 

742 input: str | list[str], 

743 ids: list[str] | None = None, 

744 file_paths: str | list[str] | None = None, 

745 track_id: str | None = None, 

746 docs_format: str = FULL_DOCS_FORMAT_RAW, 

747 parse_engine: str | list[str] | None = None, 

748 process_options: str | list[str] | None = None, 

749 chunk_options: dict | list[dict] | None = None, 

750 admission_token: str | None = None, 

751 from_scan: bool = False, 

752 ) -> str: 

753 """ 

754 Pipeline for Processing Documents 

755 

756 1. Validate ids if provided or generate MD5 hash IDs and remove duplicate contents 

757 2. Generate document initial status 

758 3. Filter out already processed documents 

759 4. Enqueue document in status 

760 

761 Args: 

762 input: Single document string or list of document strings (can be empty when docs_format is pending_parse) 

763 ids: list of unique document IDs, if not provided, MD5 hash IDs will be generated (from content or file_path). 

764 **Providing ``ids`` marks the SDK raw direct-insert path** 

765 (:meth:`LightRAG.ainsert`) and takes precedence over 

766 ``docs_format``: the documents are always enqueued as RAW 

767 — sanitized verbatim content, no parse-worker deferral — 

768 by design, not as an oversight. ``pending_parse`` is the 

769 server upload path, which never passes ``ids``. 

770 file_paths: list of file paths corresponding to each document, used for citation 

771 track_id: tracking ID for monitoring processing status 

772 docs_format: "raw" (default) or "pending_parse"; "pending_parse" defers 

773 extraction to the parse worker (content may be empty and 

774 content-dedup happens after parsing). Ignored when ``ids`` 

775 is provided (see ``ids`` above). 

776 parse_engine: file extraction engine already used or target engine for pending_parse 

777 process_options: per-document processing options string (i/t/e/!/F/R/V/P/C); 

778 accepted as a single string broadcast to every input or as a list 

779 aligned with ``input``. Stored verbatim on ``full_docs`` and 

780 mirrored to ``doc_status.metadata['process_options']``. 

781 chunk_options: per-document chunker parameter snapshot. 

782 Accepted as ``dict`` (broadcast to every input) or 

783 ``list[dict]`` (aligned with ``input``). When ``None``, 

784 each doc's snapshot is built via 

785 :func:`lightrag.parser.routing.resolve_chunk_options` 

786 from ``self.addon_params['chunker']``. Persisted to 

787 ``full_docs[doc_id]['chunk_options']`` and consumed by 

788 :meth:`process_single_document` to drive the file 

789 chunkers (F / R / V / P). Callers that need to bake 

790 F-strategy runtime args (``split_by_character`` / 

791 ``split_by_character_only``) into the snapshot — e.g. 

792 :meth:`LightRAG.ainsert` — should call 

793 :func:`resolve_chunk_options` themselves and pass the 

794 result here; this function is intentionally chunker- 

795 config agnostic. One key is NOT honored from the 

796 snapshot: ``semantic_vector.sentence_split_regex`` is 

797 re-read live from ``addon_params`` at process time and a 

798 snapshot value is discarded (logged at WARNING) — see 

799 :func:`lightrag.utils_pipeline.apply_trusted_sentence_split_regex` 

800 and GHSA-32jh-39m7-8x84. See 

801 ``docs/FileProcessingPipeline.md`` for the schema. 

802 admission_token: the pending-enqueue reservation the caller already 

803 holds (endpoints reserve one before reading the request body). 

804 With ``MAX_PENDING_DOCUMENTS > 0`` the admission guard 

805 re-weights THAT token to the deduped document count instead of 

806 registering a second reservation, so a request is never counted 

807 against itself. Leave ``None`` on the SDK path: the guard mints 

808 and releases its own short-lived reservation. 

809 from_scan: when True, the caller is the scan-owned background task 

810 that already holds ``pipeline_status["scanning"]``. Scan 

811 does additional doc_status reads during its classification 

812 phase (PROCESSED detection, FAILED-stub deletion, etc.) 

813 so external writers are blocked via 

814 ``scanning_exclusive``. Scan's own enqueues happen in 

815 its processing phase, after classification has cleared 

816 ``scanning_exclusive``, but ``from_scan=True`` is still 

817 forwarded as a defence-in-depth bypass so an unexpected 

818 scan-owned write inside the classification window is 

819 allowed through. External callers must leave this False. 

820 

821 Returns: 

822 str: tracking ID for monitoring processing status 

823 

824 Raises: 

825 RuntimeError: if a scan is in progress (and ``from_scan`` is 

826 False), or if a destructive job (clear / delete) is in 

827 flight. Concurrent indexing (``busy=True`` from the 

828 processing loop) is permitted — the running loop is 

829 notified via the ingress mailbox and picks up the 

830 newly-enqueued doc mid-batch (feeder) or at the batch 

831 boundary (quiescence decision). 

832 """ 

833 # Concurrency contract: enqueue may proceed concurrently with the 

834 # processing loop because (a) full_docs is upserted before 

835 # doc_status, so a consistency check never sees a ghost row, and 

836 # (b) the running loop observes the ingress mailbox mid-batch and 

837 # at every batch boundary, so work that arrives while busy is 

838 # picked up without a new run. Three states still block enqueue: 

839 # * ``scanning_exclusive`` — scan task is in its CLASSIFICATION 

840 # phase, reading doc_status to classify files and possibly 

841 # deleting stale stubs. Concurrent enqueue would race 

842 # against scan's reads / mutations. ``from_scan=True`` 

843 # lifts this guard for the scan task's own enqueues. 

844 # ``scanning`` alone (the processing phase) does NOT block, 

845 # identical to the upload-during-busy case. 

846 # * ``manual_freeze_requested`` — a manual retry has frozen new 

847 # ingress while it drains the pipeline to idle and exclusively 

848 # resets FAILED→PENDING (LR2 §6.1/§7.2). Also lifted by 

849 # ``from_scan=True`` (the scan owns the manual operation). 

850 # * ``destructive_busy`` — clear / delete is dropping storages 

851 # or removing input files; a concurrent write would be 

852 # silently clobbered. 

853 # 

854 # The check below is a FAST FAIL, not the guarantee: it registers 

855 # nothing, so a fence raised after it (a manual retry freezing ingress) 

856 # would not see this call at all. The same ``reject_when`` list is 

857 # re-evaluated atomically with the pending-enqueue reservation that 

858 # covers the writes — see ``_reserve_ingress_slot``. Checking here as 

859 # well is worth it because it refuses before the body is validated, 

860 # parsed and deduped. 

861 pipeline_status = await get_namespace_data( 

862 "pipeline_status", workspace=self.workspace 

863 ) 

864 pipeline_status_lock = get_namespace_lock( 

865 "pipeline_status", workspace=self.workspace 

866 ) 

867 reject_when = [] 

868 if not from_scan: 

869 reject_when.append( 

870 ( 

871 "scanning_exclusive", 

872 "Cannot enqueue while scan is classifying files; wait for the " 

873 "classification phase to finish before retrying.", 

874 ) 

875 ) 

876 # A manual retry (LR2 §6.1/§7.2) froze new ingress while it drains 

877 # the pipeline and exclusively resets FAILED→PENDING. Lifted for 

878 # ``from_scan=True`` exactly like scanning_exclusive: the scan is the 

879 # manual operation's own driver, so its enqueues must not self-block. 

880 reject_when.append( 

881 ( 

882 "manual_freeze_requested", 

883 "Cannot enqueue while a manual retry is draining the pipeline; " 

884 "wait for it to finish before retrying.", 

885 ) 

886 ) 

887 reject_when.append( 

888 ( 

889 "destructive_busy", 

890 "Cannot enqueue while pipeline is clearing or deleting documents; " 

891 "wait for the running job to finish before retrying.", 

892 ) 

893 ) 

894 mutation_result = await check_pipeline_status_mutation( 

895 pipeline_status, 

896 pipeline_status_lock, 

897 reject_when=reject_when, 

898 # A caller holding a registered pending-enqueue reservation was 

899 # admitted before any fence raised since, and the fence holder either 

900 # could not raise it while that reservation exists or is waiting for 

901 # it (LR2 §9.2). Refusing here would drop the work of a request whose 

902 # client was already told it was accepted — and for /text there is no 

903 # input file to rediscover, so the content would simply be lost. 

904 # That reasoning covers the enqueue-stall RECOVERY fence too, which 

905 # is raised by the drain that gave up waiting for these very 

906 # reservations; the exemption is applied there inside 

907 # ``check_pipeline_status_mutation``. 

908 exempt_if_reserved=admission_token, 

909 ) 

910 if not mutation_result.acquired: 

911 # Structured, not a bare message (LR2 §9.1): an SDK caller must be 

912 # able to tell a fenced workspace (503) from a bounded freeze/scan/ 

913 # destructive window worth retrying (409) without string matching. 

914 raise PipelineReservationConflictError( 

915 mutation_result.message or "pipeline reservation is unavailable", 

916 conflict=mutation_result.conflict, 

917 fence=mutation_result.fence, 

918 ) 

919 

920 # Generate track_id if not provided 

921 if track_id is None or track_id.strip() == "": 

922 track_id = generate_track_id("enqueue") 

923 if isinstance(input, str): 

924 input = [input] 

925 if isinstance(ids, str): 925 ↛ 926line 925 didn't jump to line 926 because the condition on line 925 was never true

926 ids = [ids] 

927 if isinstance(file_paths, str): 

928 file_paths = [file_paths]

2278 async def _feeder_next_batch(self, ingress) -> list[PipelineIngressMessage]: 

2279 """Block until at least one document message is available, then return 

2280 up to ``_FEEDER_DRAIN_LIMIT`` messages from the channel. 

2281 

2282 Two ingress flavors (see :mod:`lightrag.kg.pipeline_ingress`): 

2283 

2284 * single-process ``AsyncioPipelineIngress`` — fully event-driven: 

2285 ``await get_document()`` returns one message (pairing ``task_done``), 

2286 then a bounded non-blocking ``drain_documents`` sweeps up to the 

2287 remaining limit. 

2288 * multiprocess ``ManagerPipelineIngress`` — no async get; block a 

2289 worker thread in ``wait_for_documents(timeout)`` (a WAIT that never 

2290 dequeues, so a cancelled/timed-out thread cannot steal a message), 

2291 then a bounded ``drain_documents``. An empty poll returns ``[]`` and 

2292 the feeder loops. 

2293 

2294 The drain is bounded so the feeder returns to its control-signal check 

2295 instead of draining the whole 4096-deep channel in one pass, and so a 

2296 teardown re-publish never has to restore more than one bounded drain. 

2297 Cancellation propagates out of the ``await`` here (nothing dequeued 

2298 yet); a message drained but not routed is carried in the feeder's 

2299 deferred set and re-published on teardown. 

2300 """ 

2301 if hasattr(ingress, "get_document"): 2301 ↛ 2304line 2301 didn't jump to line 2304 because the condition on line 2301 was always true

2302 first = await ingress.get_document() 

2303 return [first, *ingress.drain_documents(limit=_FEEDER_DRAIN_LIMIT - 1)] 

2304 await asyncio.to_thread(ingress.wait_for_documents, _FEEDER_POLL_SECONDS) 

2305 return ingress.drain_documents(limit=_FEEDER_DRAIN_LIMIT)

2307 async def _admit_fed_document( 

2308 self, 

2309 ctx: "_BatchRunContext", 

2310 doc_id: str, 

2311 status_doc: DocProcessingStatus, 

2312 content_data: dict, 

2313 ) -> None:

2315 

2316 Fixes the ghost-inflight window: the id is registered in 

2317 ``routing_doc_ids`` (and the batch counters bumped) UNDER the lock 

2318 BEFORE the bounded-queue ``put`` — which may block and be cancelled — 

2319 and is only moved into ``inflight_doc_ids`` AFTER the put succeeds, with 

2320 no ``await`` between the discard and the add. A cancelled/failed put 

2321 rolls the registration and counters back so the document is neither 

2322 double-counted nor permanently shadowed from re-admission; the message 

2323 itself is put back to the mailbox by the feeder's teardown re-publish. 

2324 

2325 ``content_data`` is the full_docs row the caller (``_route_one``) already 

2326 read for its visibility check, reused here for engine routing so 

2327 admission does not issue a second full_docs read.

2329 file_path = getattr(status_doc, "file_path", "unknown_source")

2331 file_path=file_path, content_data=content_data or {} 

2332 ) 

2333 spec = ctx.parser_specs.get(key) 

2334 group = spec.queue_group if spec is not None else "native" 

2335 queue = ctx.parse_queues.get(group, ctx.parse_queues["native"]) 

2336 

2337 async with ctx.pipeline_status_lock: 

2338 ctx.routing_doc_ids.add(doc_id) 

2339 ctx.total_files += 1 

2340 ctx.pipeline_status["docs"] = ctx.pipeline_status.get("docs", 0) + 1 

2341 ctx.pipeline_status["batchs"] = ctx.pipeline_status.get("batchs", 0) + 1 

2342 try: 

2343 await queue.put((doc_id, status_doc)) 

2344 except BaseException:

2346 ctx.routing_doc_ids.discard(doc_id) 

2347 ctx.total_files = max(0, ctx.total_files - 1) 

2348 ctx.pipeline_status["docs"] = max( 

2349 0, ctx.pipeline_status.get("docs", 0) - 1 

2350 ) 

2351 ctx.pipeline_status["batchs"] = max( 

2352 0, ctx.pipeline_status.get("batchs", 0) - 1 

2353 ) 

2354 raise 

2355 async with ctx.pipeline_status_lock: 

2356 # No await between these two mutations: dedup never sees a gap. 

2357 ctx.routing_doc_ids.discard(doc_id) 

2358 ctx.inflight_doc_ids.add(doc_id)

2360 def _republish_documents( 

2361 self, ingress, messages, *, source: str = "feeder" 

2362 ) -> None: 

2363 """Best-effort re-publish of drained-but-unresolved document messages. 

2364 

2365 The document channel drain is destructive (``drain_documents`` removes 

2366 the messages). On a teardown — user cancel, internal error, or the 

2367 exception backoff — the drained messages this feeder had not yet routed 

2368 or confirmed stale/terminal must go back to the mailbox: a cancelled 

2369 run consumes nothing further, so without the restore those PENDING 

2370 docs would wait for an unrelated future trigger instead of the next 

2371 run. A multiprocess ``put_document`` is a Manager RPC; swallow 

2372 failures — the docs are PENDING and still recovered by the next 

2373 initial scan. 

2374 

2375 ``source`` selects the log level: the feeder path stays at debug (its 

2376 drops are per-message noise backed by auto-rescan / the next initial 

2377 scan), while the supervisor's quiescence compensation 

2378 (``"quiescence"``) logs a warning — there a swallowed drop is one of 

2379 the last lines that can attribute why a doc waited for an unrelated 

2380 trigger. 

2381 """ 

2382 log = logger.debug if source == "feeder" else logger.warning 

2383 for msg in messages: 

2384 try: 

2385 ingress.put_document(msg) 

2386 except Exception as republish_error: 

2387 log( 

2388 f"[{source}] document re-publish failed for " 

2389 f"{getattr(msg, 'doc_id', None)}: {republish_error}" 

2390 )

2411 if duplicate:

2431 def _feeder_should_yield( 

2432 self, ctx: "_BatchRunContext", ingress, *, check_auto: bool 

2433 ) -> bool: 

2434 """True when the feeder must stop admitting and let the batch reach its 

2435 quiescence point: 

2436 

2437 * cancellation requested (so ``/cancel_pipeline`` can complete); 

2438 * a sticky manual retry request waiting (so an unbounded batch does not 

2439 starve it) — both re-checked before every single admission, so the 

2440 yield latency is one admission, not a whole drain; 

2441 * (``check_auto``, at the top of each drain) the auto-rescan flag is 

2442 dirty AND this epoch is unbounded (``PIPELINE_SCHEDULING_PAGE_SIZE=0`` 

2443 disables ``_feeder_epoch_full``). 

2444 

2445 The flag is the coarse "only a strict rescan can find this work" 

2446 signal — an overflow dropped notifications, a partial upsert landed, 

2447 one of this feeder's own skips armed it, or a wake-up was refused 

2448 because this very run holds ``busy`` — and only the supervisor's 

2449 boundary rescan can serve it. But yielding does NOT bring that 

2450 boundary closer on its own: the boundary is the queue-join cascade in 

2451 :meth:`_run_pipeline_batch` (which then cancels this feeder), and a 

2452 feeder parked on ``wait_for_documents`` holds no unfinished queue 

2453 item, so it never delays a join. The ONLY way the feeder can postpone 

2454 the boundary is by admitting new work indefinitely — and with paging 

2455 on, ``_feeder_epoch_full`` already caps that at 

2456 ``PIPELINE_SCHEDULING_PAGE_SIZE`` admissions per epoch, so the flag is 

2457 served within one bounded epoch. Yielding on it as well buys nothing 

2458 and costs the accelerator: every per-file ``/upload`` calls 

2459 ``apipeline_process_enqueue_documents`` after its enqueue, each such 

2460 call is refused while a batch runs, and each refusal arms this flag 

2461 (see ``acquire_processing_reservation``) — so a bare-flag yield killed 

2462 the feeder for the rest of the batch on the SECOND uploaded file and 

2463 stranded every later file in the mailbox until the batch barrier. 

2464 

2465 With paging disabled there is no admission cap, so a sustained stream 

2466 could keep this epoch alive forever; there the dirty flag still 

2467 yields. 

2468 

2469 The feeder only PEEKS the flag (via ``counts``); the supervisor 

2470 remains its sole consumer. 

2471 

2472 NOT ``has_work()`` — that would busy-loop on a pending manual/auto entry. 

2473 """ 

2474 if ctx.pipeline_cancel_event is not None and ctx.pipeline_cancel_event.is_set(): 

2475 return True 

2476 if ingress.peek_next_manual_retry() is not None: 

2477 return True 

2478 if ( 

2479 check_auto 

2480 and getattr(self, "pipeline_scheduling_page_size", 0) <= 0 

2481 and ingress.counts().get("auto_rescan_pending") 

2482 ): 

2483 return True 

2484 return False 

2485 

2486 def _feeder_epoch_full(self, ctx: "_BatchRunContext") -> bool: 

2487 """True when this epoch has admitted ``PIPELINE_SCHEDULING_PAGE_SIZE`` 

2488 documents (``inflight`` + ``routing``) — the single-epoch bound of 

2489 LR2 §6.4. 

2490 

2491 ``inflight_doc_ids`` grows monotonically within a batch (it is the 

2492 dedup set of everything routed into this epoch, never shrunk on 

2493 completion), so this counts total admissions this epoch, not live 

2494 concurrency. Once the count reaches the page size the feeder stops 

2495 admitting and the remaining mailbox / doc_status work continues in the 

2496 NEXT epoch (a fresh page via CONTINUE_SWEEP_PAGE, or a CONTINUE_DOCUMENT 

2497 refetch). Disabled when paging is off (``page_size <= 0``) — the feeder 

2498 then admits freely, exactly as before Phase 2. Read without the lock: a 

2499 single-threaded ``len`` is a consistent snapshot and this is a soft 

2500 backpressure gate, not a hard invariant. 

2501 """ 

2502 page_size = getattr(self, "pipeline_scheduling_page_size", 0) 

2503 if page_size <= 0: 

2504 return False 

2505 return len(ctx.inflight_doc_ids) + len(ctx.routing_doc_ids) >= page_size

2507 async def _pipeline_feeder(self, ctx: "_BatchRunContext", ingress) -> None: 

2508 """Route documents that arrive DURING a batch into its parse queues so 

2509 they process without waiting for the batch barrier. 

2510 

2511 Pure accelerator: every message it discards or skips is a PENDING 

2512 ``doc_status`` row that the supervisor's quiescence rescan or the 

2513 next run's initial strict scan recovers. The feeder never writes 

2514 ``doc_status``; correctness is anchored by the doc_status source of 

2515 truth plus the atomic quiescence decision — the feeder only removes 

2516 latency. 

2517 

2518 Per drained message: ROUTED (admitted), STALE/TERMINAL (dropped), or 

2519 SKIPPED (full_docs not yet visible / a transient read — arms the 

2520 auto-rescan flag; re-published on a teardown, see ``_route_one`` and 

2521 ``_republish_documents``). 

2522 

2523 **Bounded liveness (yields to control signals):** the feeder stops 

2524 admitting — returns so the batch drains to its quiescence point — when 

2525 cancellation is requested (otherwise ``/cancel_pipeline`` could never 

2526 complete under a sustained upload stream that keeps the parse queue 

2527 non-empty) or when a sticky manual retry request is waiting (it is only 

2528 consumed at the batch boundary, so an unbounded batch would starve it), 

2529 or — only with paging disabled, where nothing else caps this epoch's 

2530 admissions — when the auto-rescan flag is dirty. 

2531 This is re-checked before the drain AND before EVERY admission 

2532 (:meth:`_feeder_should_yield`), so a signal that lands while the feeder 

2533 is admitting a full drain is honored within one admission, not after up 

2534 to ``_FEEDER_DRAIN_LIMIT`` more. It deliberately does NOT wait on 

2535 ``has_work()`` — that would busy-loop on a pending manual/auto signal. 

2536 

2537 **Deferred survives the whole feeder:** SKIPPED messages and a drain's 

2538 unrouted tail accumulate in a feeder-lifetime ``deferred`` list and are 

2539 re-published to the mailbox on ANY exit (the ``finally``) — the drain 

2540 already removed them from the mailbox, so a skip forgotten from an 

2541 earlier iteration would otherwise be lost on a cancelled run (which 

2542 consumes nothing further). An unexpected per-iteration failure logs, 

2543 re-publishes just that drain's tail for retry, backs off, and continues 

2544 rather than silently dying for the rest of the batch. 

2545 """ 

2546 # Feeder-lifetime set: SKIPs (full_docs not yet visible / transient read) 

2547 # and any drained-but-unrouted tail. Restored to the mailbox on exit. 

2548 deferred: list = [] 

2549 try: 

2550 while True: 

2551 batch: list = [] 

2552 reached = 0 

2553 try: 

2554 # Top-of-drain yield check is INSIDE the try so a transient 

2555 # manual-peek / counts RPC failure (multiprocess) is logged 

2556 # and retried, not left to silently kill the feeder. Includes 

2557 # the auto-rescan flag ONLY when this epoch is unbounded — 

2558 # with paging on, the epoch cap below is what bounds the 

2559 # batch, and a busy-refused upload wake-up arms that flag on 

2560 # every file (see _feeder_should_yield). 

2561 if self._feeder_should_yield(ctx, ingress, check_auto=True): 

2562 return 

2563 # Single-epoch bound (LR2 §6.4): once this batch holds 

2564 # PIPELINE_SCHEDULING_PAGE_SIZE docs the feeder stops 

2565 # admitting; the rest continues in the next epoch (a fresh 

2566 # page, or a CONTINUE_DOCUMENT refetch of the mailbox). 

2567 if self._feeder_epoch_full(ctx): 

2568 return 

2569 batch = await self._feeder_next_batch(ingress) 

2570 drained_ids = [msg.doc_id for msg in batch if msg.doc_id] 

2571 if drained_ids: 2571 ↛ 2603line 2571 didn't jump to line 2603 because the condition on line 2571 was always true

2572 # Bounded to THIS drain's ids (not the whole PENDING 

2573 # set): hydrate full status, keep only rows still 

2574 # PENDING. A drained doc now processed/failed/deleted is 

2575 # simply absent, and _route_one drops it as stale. 

2576 hydrated = await self.doc_status.get_full_docs_by_ids( 

2577 drained_ids, strict=True 

2578 ) 

2579 pending = { 

2580 doc_id: doc 

2581 for doc_id, doc in hydrated.items() 

2582 if getattr(doc, "status", None) == DocStatus.PENDING 

2583 } 

2584 for reached, msg in enumerate(batch): 

2585 # Honor an in-flight cancel/manual WITHIN one doc 

2586 # (auto-rescan is coarser — checked per drain above). 

2587 if self._feeder_should_yield( 

2588 ctx, ingress, check_auto=False 

2589 ): 

2590 deferred.extend(batch[reached:]) # unprocessed tail 

2591 return 

2592 # Re-check the epoch bound mid-drain: earlier 

2593 # admissions in THIS loop may have reached the cap. 

2594 if self._feeder_epoch_full(ctx): 2594 ↛ 2595line 2594 didn't jump to line 2595 because the condition on line 2594 was never true

2595 deferred.extend(batch[reached:]) 

2596 return 

2597 if not await self._route_one(ctx, msg, pending): 

2598 deferred.append(msg) # SKIP — survives to teardown 

2599 # Arm the recovery signal so the skip is picked up 

2600 # by the supervisor's next rescan even if this 

2601 # feeder never otherwise reaches a boundary. 

2602 _rearm_auto_rescan(ingress) 

2603 reached = len(batch) # every message reached a decision 

2604 except asyncio.CancelledError: 

2605 deferred.extend(batch[reached:]) # unprocessed tail → finally 

2606 raise 

2607 except Exception as feeder_error: 

2608 logger.warning( 

2609 "[feeder] in-batch feeder iteration failed (batch " 

2610 f"continues; re-published messages recover docs): {feeder_error}" 

2611 ) 

2612 # Retry just this drain's unprocessed tail; the accumulated 

2613 # deferred skips are restored on exit, not bounced each error. 

2614 self._republish_documents(ingress, batch[reached:]) 

2615 await asyncio.sleep(_FEEDER_POLL_SECONDS) 

2616 finally: 

2617 self._republish_documents(ingress, deferred)

2619 async def _run_pipeline_batch( 

2620 self, 

2621 to_process_docs: dict[str, DocProcessingStatus], 

2622 *, 

2623 pipeline_status: dict, 

2624 pipeline_status_lock, 

2625 ingress, 

2626 token: str | None = None, 

2627 ) -> None: 

2628 """Run one batch of pending documents through the parse → analyze → 

2629 process queues. 

2630 

2631 Three cascading layers of queues: 

2632 - Layer 1: Content Parsing (parse_native / parse_mineru / parse_docling) 

2633 - Layer 2: Multimodal Analyze (analyze_multimodal) 

2634 - Layer 3: Entity / Relation Extraction (process_single_document) 

2635 """ 

2636 total_files = len(to_process_docs) 

2637 pipeline_status["job_name"] = self._format_job_name( 

2638 to_process_docs, total_files

2706 s.engine_name

2722 for s in parser_specs.values()

3818 async def _decide_pipeline_next_step(

3827 

3828 Closes the loop-exit handoff race: a publisher that lands a signal 

3829 (sticky manual request, auto-rescan flag, or a document message) 

3830 while the processing loop is on its way out is observed in the same 

3831 critical section that would release ``busy``, so the loop refetches 

3832 instead of stranding the new work.

3834 Fixed priority (LR2 §6.2): cancellation → advancement of the CURRENT 

3835 manual drain/reset → earliest (new) manual request → auto-rescan → 

3836 document mailbox → release. The lock covers only this decision (mailbox 

3837 calls are single in-memory/Manager RPCs; storage queries happen strictly 

3838 outside, in :meth:`_refetch_for_decision`).

3841 under this same lock): 

3842 

3843 * **DRAIN_TO_IDLE** — this run already holds the freeze and is draining 

3844 for a manual retry. Advancing THAT drain is top priority after cancel: 

3845 finish the AUTO sweep pages, consume auto-rescan / document backlog, 

3846 then wait for pre-freeze in-flight enqueues (CONTINUE_DRAIN_WAIT), and 

3847 once strictly idle enter the exclusive reset (BEGIN_EXCLUSIVE_RESET). 

3848 A second manual is NOT peeked here — it waits FIFO until this one ACKs 

3849 and the phase returns to IDLE (LR2 §7.5). 

3850 * **IDLE** — normal quiescence: 

3851 0. **Cancellation** (consumes NOTHING): the cancel endpoint sets the 

3852 flag under this same lock, so a cancel never lands between its 

3853 check and a consuming step below. 

3854 1. **Manual retry** (peeked, NOT consumed): earliest sticky request; 

3855 BEGINS a drain (CONTINUE_MANUAL sets the freeze). It preempts an 

3856 in-progress AUTO sweep (the drain re-scans AUTO from Start, so no 

3857 doc is lost). Stays sticky, ACKed only after the exclusive reset. 

3858 2. **Sweep page** — the in-progress bounded AUTO sweep has more pages. 

3859 3. **Auto rescan** (consumed atomically): sole consumer of the dirty 

3860 flag; re-armed on a failed follow-up query in the refetch. 

3861 4. **Document channel non-empty** (peeked, NOT drained). 

3862 5. Nothing pending: release the slot with its owner token — RELEASED.

3864 Boundary (documented, not solved here): this closes every 

3865 published-but-missed handoff, but an enqueue that crashes BETWEEN its 

3866 doc_status persist and its publish leaves no signal at all — that doc 

3867 is recovered by the next run's initial strict scan, never by this 

3868 decision.

3873 PipelineNextStep.CANCELLED, 

3874 internal_error=pipeline_status.get("cancellation_reason")

3878 pipeline_status.get("manual_phase", MANUAL_PHASE_IDLE)

3884 # manual — a second request waits FIFO (LR2 §7.5).

3892 # Enqueues reserved BEFORE the freeze must finish (their 

3893 # PENDING docs join this cohort) before the reset can start 

3894 # with no failed producer (LR2 §7.2 step 5 / §7.3). The 

3895 # CONTINUE_DRAIN_WAIT refetch reaps confirmed-dead tokens 

3896 # before it waits, so a worker SIGKILLed mid-reserve (Linux

4162 ``/documents/scan`` that fixes this) but the reasoning was wrong: a sticky 

4163 un-ACKed manual request already makes ``/scan`` refuse its reservation 

4164 (``refuse_when_manual_pending``, LR2 §8.1, so a scan cannot jump the manual 

4165 FIFO), and the blocker leaves exactly that request queued. So the 

4166 "unfenced" path had no reachable remedy either — it was a silent dead end 

4167 instead of a loud one, which is strictly worse. 

4168 

4169 The way out is therefore the same for both halves of the deadlock and is 

4170 documented on the fence: ``POST /documents/recovery/force_reset`` clears the 

4171 fence AND cancels the queued manual intents that were blocking ``/scan``, 

4172 after which ``POST /documents/scan`` rolls the journal back and runs the 

4173 FAILED reset itself. 

4174 

4175 Raises :class:`PipelineRecoveryRequiredError`, which unwinds the run 

4176 through its ``finally``: freeze and ``busy`` are released (owner-checked) so 

4177 a live-but-exiting owner never wedges the pipeline, while the fence 

4178 survives to refuse mutations with 503. 

4179 """ 

4180 detail = ( 

4181 f"manual retry cannot start: {len(blocking_ids)} or more active " 

4182 "document(s) hold an unfinished custom-chunk operation, so the " 

4183 "pipeline is not idle and the exclusive FAILED reset must not begin. " 

4184 "Clear this with POST /documents/recovery/force_reset (which also " 

4185 "cancels the queued retry that is blocking /documents/scan), then POST " 

4186 "/documents/scan to roll the operation back — the scan runs the FAILED " 

4187 f"reset itself (blocked doc id sample: {', '.join(blocking_ids) or 'unavailable'})." 

4188 ) 

4189 logger.error(detail) 

4190 await fence_workspace_for_recovery( 

4191 pipeline_status, 

4192 pipeline_status_lock, 

4193 kind="manual_drain_blocked", 

4194 message=detail, 

4195 operation_record={"scope": ", ".join(blocking_ids)}, 

4196 ) 

4197 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

4198 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = detail 

4199 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, detail) 

4200 raise PipelineRecoveryRequiredError(detail, blocked_doc_ids=tuple(blocking_ids))

4202 async def _fence_stalled_manual_drain( 

4203 self,

4213 design's rule applies: set ``recovery_required``, report a BOUNDED sample 

4214 of the blocking doc ids, and stop — never spin, and never silently drop

4218 through its ``finally``: the freeze and ``busy`` are released

4223 consumed by an attempt that never ran.

4226 detail = ( 

4227 f"manual retry drain stalled: {len(docs)} active document(s) have " 

4228 f"blocked DRAIN_TO_IDLE for {_MANUAL_DRAIN_STALL_ROUNDS} consecutive " 

4229 f"rounds without changing state (blocked doc id sample: " 

4230 f"{', '.join(blocked) or 'unavailable'})." 

4231 ) 

4232 logger.error(detail) 

4233 await fence_workspace_for_recovery( 

4234 pipeline_status, 

4235 pipeline_status_lock, 

4236 kind="manual_drain_stalled", 

4237 message=detail, 

4238 operation_record={"scope": ", ".join(blocked)}, 

4239 ) 

4240 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

4241 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = detail 

4242 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, detail) 

4243 raise PipelineRecoveryRequiredError(detail, blocked_doc_ids=tuple(blocked))

4245 async def _fence_stalled_enqueue_drain( 

4246 self, 

4247 live_tokens: dict[str, Any], 

4248 pipeline_status: dict, 

4249 pipeline_status_lock, 

4250 ) -> None: 

4251 """Fence a DRAIN_TO_IDLE whose in-flight enqueue set never drains. 

4252 

4253 The same ``pending_enqueue_tokens`` have held the drain for 

4254 :data:`_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` without one of them 

4255 finishing. The freeze admits no new reservation, so the set can only 

4256 shrink; a set that has not shrunk for that long is not a producer being 

4257 slow, it is a producer that will never release. 

4258 

4259 The canonical way in was a bg task that kept its own reservation while 

4260 driving ``apipeline_process_enqueue_documents``: the run then waited on a 

4261 token only it could release, and only by returning — which it could not 

4262 do until the wait ended. That specific self-deadlock is closed at the 

4263 source (``_release_admission_after_enqueue`` in the API layer releases 

4264 between enqueue and processing); this fence is the backstop for every 

4265 other way a holder can stop existing without releasing, and for any 

4266 future caller that reintroduces the same shape. 

4267 

4268 Fencing loses information — a live-but-slow producer is refused with 503 

4269 from here on — and that cost is accepted deliberately: the alternative 

4270 this replaces is an unbounded wait with ``busy`` latched, NO fence for 

4271 ``POST /documents/recovery/force_reset`` to clear, and a process restart 

4272 as the only remedy. See :data:`_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`. 

4273 

4274 Raises :class:`PipelineRecoveryRequiredError`, which unwinds the run 

4275 through its ``finally``: freeze and ``busy`` are released (owner-checked) 

4276 so the latch is gone even though the fence survives to refuse mutations. 

4277 The manual request stays sticky and un-ACKed, so no FAILED document is 

4278 consumed by an attempt that never ran. 

4279 

4280 Fencing does not void the holders it names: a registered token is exempt 

4281 from this fence kind alone, so a producer that comes back still lands 

4282 its documents (see ``_stall_fence_exempts_reserved_token``). The fence 

4283 stops the workspace, not the work already admitted into it. 

4284 

4285 It does NOT raise — and does not fence — when the in-flight set changed 

4286 between the poll that observed the stall and the write that would fence 

4287 it: ``live_tokens`` was read under an EARLIER lock hold, and a producer 

4288 that releases in that gap has just proved the drain can still advance. 

4289 The caller simply waits again; the next poll sees a different set, which 

4290 resets :meth:`_ManualDrainProgress.observe_enqueue`'s counter. Fencing 

4291 from the stale snapshot would refuse every mutation on a workspace that 

4292 had already recovered, and only a manual ``force_reset`` undoes that. 

4293 """ 

4294 sample = sorted(live_tokens)[:_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SAMPLE] 

4295 owners = sorted( 

4296 { 

4297 str(meta.get("pid")) 

4298 for meta in live_tokens.values() 

4299 if isinstance(meta, Mapping) and meta.get("pid") is not None 

4300 } 

4301 ) 

4302 # Retained guards decide the remedy, so they are counted BEFORE the 

4303 # message is written: ``force_reset`` drops the ordinary enqueues out of 

4304 # this set but keeps a source-conflict repair's guard, and telling an 

4305 # operator to re-issue the retry straight away while one is held would 

4306 # only buy them another whole window and another fence. 

4307 guards = sum( 

4308 1 

4309 for meta in live_tokens.values() 

4310 if reservation_kind(meta) != ENQUEUE_RESERVATION_KIND 

4311 ) 

4312 enqueues = len(live_tokens) - guards 

4313 if guards: 

4314 remedy = ( 

4315 f"POST /documents/recovery/force_reset clears this fence, cancels " 

4316 f"the queued retry and drops the {enqueues} upload/insert " 

4317 f"reservation(s), but it does NOT drop the {guards} " 

4318 "source-conflict repair guard(s) — dropping one could corrupt " 

4319 "source ownership while its commit resumes. Wait for that repair " 

4320 "to finish, or restart the process holding it, BEFORE re-issuing " 

4321 "POST /documents/reprocess_failed: re-issuing while a guard is " 

4322 "held only stalls the drain again." 

4323 ) 

4324 else: 

4325 remedy = ( 

4326 "Clear this with POST /documents/recovery/force_reset, which " 

4327 "cancels the queued retry AND drops these reservations (an " 

4328 "upload that was merely slow is recovered by POST " 

4329 "/documents/scan; a /documents/text(s) must be re-sent), then " 

4330 "re-issue POST /documents/reprocess_failed." 

4331 ) 

4332 # API-VISIBLE, and therefore free of reservation tokens and owner pids: 

4333 # this text reaches ``recovery_message`` (``describe_recovery_fence``), 

4334 # ``latest_message`` and ``history_messages``, none of which is filtered 

4335 # further. Those three are the sanitized window the /documents/ 

4336 # pipeline_status projection exists to keep clean — it drops the whole 

4337 # internal fence record precisely so tokens and pids do not leave the 

4338 # process. The identities go to the server log below instead. 

4339 detail = ( 

4340 f"manual retry drain stalled: {len(live_tokens)} in-flight enqueue " 

4341 f"reservation(s) ({enqueues} upload/insert, {guards} source-conflict " 

4342 "repair guard(s)) have blocked DRAIN_TO_IDLE for " 

4343 f"{_MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:.0f}s without one of them " 

4344 "finishing, and the freeze admits no new ones, so waiting again " 

4345 f"cannot change the count. {remedy} The holders' process identities " 

4346 "are in the server log." 

4347 ) 

4348 observed = set(live_tokens) 

4349 

4350 def _set_unchanged(snapshot: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool: 

4351 # Any difference counts, in either direction: a set that is not the 

4352 # one observed is not the evidence this stall verdict was reached 

4353 # on. Under the freeze it can only shrink, but a future reservation 

4354 # kind the freeze does not refuse must not be able to grow it into 

4355 # a fence either. 

4356 return set(snapshot.get("pending_enqueue_tokens") or {}) == observed 

4357 

4358 # Nothing is logged at error level before this returns: a refused 

4359 # precondition is a drain that recovered, not a fault. 

4360 if not await fence_workspace_for_recovery( 

4361 pipeline_status, 

4362 pipeline_status_lock, 

4363 kind=MANUAL_DRAIN_ENQUEUE_STALL_FENCE, 

4364 message=detail, 

4365 operation_record={"scope": ", ".join(sample)}, 

4366 precondition=_set_unchanged, 

4367 ): 

4368 logger.warning( 

4369 "[pipeline] manual retry drain looked stalled on " 

4370 f"{len(observed)} in-flight enqueue reservation(s), but the set " 

4371 "changed before the fence was written (a producer finished, or a " 

4372 "dead holder was reaped), so the drain keeps waiting instead of " 

4373 "fencing the workspace." 

4374 ) 

4375 return 

4376 

4377 # The log is the one surface that may carry the credentials: it is 

4378 # server-side, and an operator restarting a wedged holder needs its pid. 

4379 logger.error( 

4380 f"{detail} (reservation token sample: " 

4381 f"{', '.join(sample) or 'unavailable'}; owner pid(s): " 

4382 f"{', '.join(owners) or 'unavailable'})" 

4383 ) 

4384 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

4385 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = detail 

4386 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, detail) 

4387 raise PipelineRecoveryRequiredError(detail)
