5681 # leaving it inline would keep /health stalled over exactly 

5682 # the window this work exists to free. One coarse submission, 

5683 # not one per chunk: the executor has a single worker and the 

5684 # backfill mutates ``chunking_result`` in place. 

5685 await run_in_chunking_executor( 

5686 backfill_chunk_sidecars, chunking_result, blocks_path 

5687 ) 

5688 

5689 chunks = build_chunks_dict_from_chunking_result( 

5690 chunking_result, doc_id=doc_id, file_path=file_path 

5691 ) 

5692 

5693 if not chunks: 

5694 logger.warning("No document chunks to process") 

5695 

5696 process_start_time = int(time.time()) 

5697 

5698 await self._raise_if_cancelled( 

5699 ctx.pipeline_status, ctx.pipeline_status_lock 

5700 ) 

5701 

5702 # Stage 1: persist doc_status PROCESSING + chunks in parallel. 

5703 doc_status_task = asyncio.create_task( 

5704 self._upsert_doc_status_transition( 

5705 ctx=ctx, 

5706 doc_id=doc_id, 

5707 status=DocStatus.PROCESSING, 

5708 status_doc=status_doc, 

5709 file_path=file_path, 

5710 extra_fields={ 

5711 "chunks_count": len(chunks), 

5712 "chunks_list": list(chunks.keys()), 

5713 }, 

5714 metadata_extra={ 

5715 "process_start_time": process_start_time, 

5716 **extraction_meta, 

5717 }, 

5718 ) 

5719 ) 

5720 chunks_vdb_task = asyncio.create_task(self.chunks_vdb.upsert(chunks)) 

5721 text_chunks_task = asyncio.create_task(self.text_chunks.upsert(chunks)) 

5722 first_stage_tasks = [ 

5723 doc_status_task, 

5724 chunks_vdb_task, 

5725 text_chunks_task, 

5726 ] 

5727 entity_relation_task = None 

5728 

5729 await asyncio.gather(*first_stage_tasks) 

5730 

5731 # Stage 2: entity/relation extraction (after text_chunks are 

5732 # saved). When the user opted out via process_options '!', 

5733 # skip extraction entirely; chunks remain in the vector 

5734 # store so naive / mix retrieval still works. 

5735 if doc_process_opts.skip_kg: 

5736 logger.info( 

5737 f"[skip_kg] process_options '!' set for d-id: {doc_id}; " 

5738 f"skipping entity/relation extraction" 

5739 ) 

5740 chunk_results = [] 

5741 extraction_meta["skip_kg"] = True 

5742 else: 

5743 entity_relation_task = asyncio.create_task( 

5744 self._process_extract_entities( 

5745 chunks, 

5746 ctx.pipeline_status, 

5747 ctx.pipeline_status_lock, 

5748 truncation_tally=truncation_tally, 

5749 ) 

5750 ) 

5751 chunk_results = await entity_relation_task 

5752 file_extraction_stage_ok = True 

5753 

5754 except Exception as e: 

5755 pending_tasks = first_stage_tasks + ( 

5756 [entity_relation_task] if entity_relation_task else [] 

5757 ) 

5758 await self._finalize_doc_failure( 

5759 ctx=ctx, 

5760 doc_id=doc_id, 

5761 status_doc=status_doc, 

5762 file_path=file_path, 

5763 error=e, 

5764 stage_label="extract", 

5765 current_file_number=current_file_number, 

5766 total_files=ctx.total_files, 

5767 failed_chunks_snapshot=get_failed_chunk_snapshot(), 

5768 pending_tasks=pending_tasks, 

5769 metadata_extra={ 

5770 "process_start_time": process_start_time, 

5771 "process_end_time": int(time.time()), 

5772 # Same payload the merge-stage failure below writes. 

5773 # None of these keys is carried over, so omitting them 

5774 # here DROPPED the parse_format / parse_engine / 

5775 # chunk_method / mm_chunks fields that the PROCESSING 

5776 # transition had just stamped: a document that failed 

5777 # during extraction ended up describing itself less 

5778 # than one that failed one stage later. Always bound — 

5779 # initialised empty above the try, so a failure that 

5780 # precedes chunking simply contributes nothing. 

5781 **extraction_meta, 

5782 # A run that truncated and then failed keeps the 

5783 # evidence: truncation is often why it failed. 

5784 **truncation_metadata_extra(), 

5785 }, 

5786 pipeline_status=ctx.pipeline_status, 

5787 pipeline_status_lock=ctx.pipeline_status_lock, 

5788 ) 

5789 

5790 # Concurrency is controlled by keyed lock for individual 

5791 # entities and relationships. 

5792 if file_extraction_stage_ok: 

5793 try: 

5794 await self._raise_if_cancelled( 

5795 ctx.pipeline_status, ctx.pipeline_status_lock 

5796 ) 

5797 

5798 # Use chunk_results from entity_relation_task. When 

5799 # skip_kg is set, chunk_results is empty so there are no 

5800 # nodes/edges to merge — but we still need to flush the 

5801 # chunks_vdb / text_chunks writes (already done above) 

5802 # and reach PROCESSED. 

5803 if not doc_process_opts.skip_kg: 

5804 await merge_nodes_and_edges( 

5805 chunk_results=chunk_results, 

5806 knowledge_graph_inst=self.chunk_entity_relation_graph, 

5807 entity_vdb=self.entities_vdb, 

5808 relationships_vdb=self.relationships_vdb, 

5809 global_config=self._build_global_config(), 

5810 full_entities_storage=self.full_entities, 

5811 full_relations_storage=self.full_relations, 

5812 doc_id=doc_id, 

5813 pipeline_status=ctx.pipeline_status, 

5814 pipeline_status_lock=ctx.pipeline_status_lock, 

5815 llm_response_cache=self.llm_response_cache, 

5816 entity_chunks_storage=self.entity_chunks, 

5817 relation_chunks_storage=self.relation_chunks, 

5818 current_file_number=current_file_number, 

5819 total_files=ctx.total_files, 

5820 file_path=file_path, 

5821 on_anchors_durable=partial( 

5822 self._mark_graph_mutation_started, doc_id, status_doc 

5823 ), 

5824 truncation_tally=truncation_tally, 

5825 ) 

5826 

5827 # If another in-flight document already triggered an abort 

5828 # (e.g. a storage flush error set cancellation_requested), 

5829 # do not mark PROCESSED or re-run _insert_done here: the 

5830 # shared flush buffer is being torn down, so re-flushing 

5831 # would just re-raise the same error. Bail out as cancelled 

5832 # so this document is FAILED and retried on the next run. 

5833 await self._raise_if_cancelled( 

5834 ctx.pipeline_status, ctx.pipeline_status_lock 

5835 ) 

5836 

5837 # Flush ALL derived stores BEFORE the durable PROCESSED 

5838 # write. doc_status backends persist immediately on 

5839 # upsert, so writing PROCESSED first opens a crash window 

5840 # where the status is durable but the graph/vector/chunk 

5841 # data is not — a false PROCESSED that recovery can never 

5842 # detect (status is the commit record). 

5843 await self._insert_done() 

5844 

5845 # A sibling document's flush error may have aborted the 

5846 # batch while our flush ran; do not mark PROCESSED during 

5847 # teardown — bail out so this document is FAILED and 

5848 # retried on the next run. 

5849 await self._raise_if_cancelled( 

5850 ctx.pipeline_status, ctx.pipeline_status_lock 

5851 ) 

5852 

5853 process_end_time = int(time.time()) 

5854 await self._upsert_doc_status_transition( 

5855 ctx=ctx, 

5856 doc_id=doc_id, 

5857 status=DocStatus.PROCESSED, 

5858 status_doc=status_doc, 

5859 file_path=file_path, 

5860 extra_fields={ 

5861 "chunks_count": len(chunks), 

5862 "chunks_list": list(chunks.keys()), 

5863 }, 

5864 metadata_extra={ 

5865 "process_start_time": process_start_time, 

5866 "process_end_time": process_end_time, 

5867 **extraction_meta, 

5868 # Empty on a clean run, which is what CLEARS a 

5869 # previous attempt's summary: the key is not in the 

5870 # carry-over whitelist, so absence means "this 

5871 # attempt did not truncate", never "unchanged". 

5872 **truncation_metadata_extra(), 

5873 }, 

5874 # A PROCESSED document has no purge in flight by 

5875 # definition, so retire any journal that a resume purge 

5876 # left behind. Belt-and-braces next to 

5877 # _clear_kg_purge_journal: a surviving ``completed`` 

5878 # journal would name a stale operation id and collide 

5879 # with the next purge of this document. 

5880 # kg_write_state is deliberately NOT dropped — it is 

5881 # monotonic history, and the anchors written during this 

5882 # run are the proof from here on. 

5883 metadata_drop=(KG_PURGE_METADATA_KEY,), 

5884 ) 

5885 

5886 async with ctx.pipeline_status_lock: 

5887 log_message = ( 

5888 f"Completed processing file " 

5889 f"{current_file_number}/{ctx.total_files}: " 

5890 f"{file_path}" 

5891 ) 

5892 logger.info(log_message) 

5893 ctx.pipeline_status["latest_message"] = log_message 

5894 append_pipeline_history(ctx.pipeline_status, log_message) 

5895 

5896 except Exception as e: 

5897 # A storage flush failure (raised by _insert_done) is not 

5898 # attributable to this document: index_done_callback flushes 

5899 # a buffer shared across concurrently-processed files. We 

5900 # cannot tell whose record failed, so continuing risks 

5901 # marking other in-flight files PROCESSED with missing data. 

5902 # Abort the whole batch via the cooperative cancellation 

5903 # flag, tagging it as an internal error with the driver name 

5904 # and root cause so it is distinguishable from a user cancel. 

5905 if isinstance(e, IndexFlushError): 

5906 async with ctx.pipeline_status_lock: 

5907 ctx.pipeline_status.update( 

5908 { 

5909 "cancellation_requested": True, 

5910 "cancellation_reason": "internal_error", 

5911 "cancellation_detail": ( 

5912 f"{e.storage_name}[{e.namespace}]: " 

5913 f"{e.__cause__}" 

5914 ), 

5915 } 

5916 ) 

5917 logger.error( 

5918 f"Aborting pipeline batch due to storage flush error: {e}" 

5919 ) 

5920 await self._finalize_doc_failure( 

5921 ctx=ctx, 

5922 doc_id=doc_id, 

5923 status_doc=status_doc, 

5924 file_path=file_path, 

5925 error=e, 

5926 stage_label="merge", 

5927 current_file_number=current_file_number, 

5928 total_files=ctx.total_files, 

5929 failed_chunks_snapshot=get_failed_chunk_snapshot(), 

5930 pending_tasks=[], 

5931 metadata_extra={ 

5932 "process_start_time": process_start_time, 

5933 "process_end_time": int(time.time()), 

5934 **extraction_meta, 

5935 **truncation_metadata_extra(), 

5936 }, 

5937 pipeline_status=ctx.pipeline_status, 

5938 pipeline_status_lock=ctx.pipeline_status_lock, 

5939 ) 

5940 

5941 async def _purge_stale_extraction_if_resuming( 

5942 self, 

5943 *, 

5944 doc_id: str, 

5945 status_doc: DocProcessingStatus, 

5946 file_path: str, 

5947 content_data: dict[str, Any] | None, 

5948 pipeline_status: dict, 

5949 pipeline_status_lock, 

5950 ) -> None: 

5951 """If the document already has extracted content, purge stale chunks 

5952 and KG contributions before re-running chunking + entity extraction 

5953 under the current ``process_options``. 

5954 

5955 Mutates ``status_doc.chunks_list`` / ``chunks_count`` to reflect the 

5956 purge so subsequent state-machine upserts don't write back stale IDs. 

5957 Also emits an engine-mismatch warning when the filename hint disagrees 

5958 with the stored ``parse_engine`` — the extracted content is the source 

5959 of truth, so the user must delete + re-upload to switch engines. 

5960 """ 

5961 content_already_extracted = isinstance(content_data, dict) and ( 

5962 ( 

5963 content_data.get("parse_format") == FULL_DOCS_FORMAT_LIGHTRAG 

5964 and content_data.get("sidecar_location") 

5965 ) 

5966 or ( 

5967 content_data.get("parse_format") == FULL_DOCS_FORMAT_RAW 

5968 and (content_data.get("content") or "").strip() 

5969 ) 

5970 ) 

5971 if not content_already_extracted: 

5972 return 

5973 

5974 from lightrag.parser.routing import normalize_parser_engine 

5975 

5976 intended_engine, _ = resolve_file_parser_directives(file_path) 

5977 # ``parse_engine`` may carry encoded params; compare bare engine names. 

5978 stored_engine = normalize_parser_engine(content_data.get("parse_engine")) 

5979 if intended_engine and stored_engine and intended_engine != stored_engine: 

5980 log_message = ( 

5981 f"[resume] {doc_id}: filename hint / " 

5982 f"LIGHTRAG_PARSER implies engine=" 

5983 f"{intended_engine!r} but full_docs " 

5984 f"already has parse_engine=" 

5985 f"{stored_engine!r}; keeping the existing " 

5986 f"extraction. Delete + re-upload to " 

5987 f"switch engines." 

5988 ) 

5989 logger.warning(log_message) 

5990 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

5991 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = log_message 

5992 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, log_message) 

5993 

5994 # Order-preserving dedup; keep a list so it satisfies the storage delete 

5995 # contract (``delete(ids: list[str])``) when passed down to purge. 

5996 stored_chunk_ids = list( 

5997 dict.fromkeys( 

5998 chunk_id 

5999 for chunk_id in (status_doc.chunks_list or []) 

6000 if isinstance(chunk_id, str) and chunk_id 

6001 ) 

6002 ) 

6003 if not stored_chunk_ids: 

6004 return 

6005 

6006 log_message = ( 

6007 f"[resume] {doc_id}: purging " 

6008 f"{len(stored_chunk_ids)} chunk(s) and " 

6009 f"associated KG entries from a previous run " 

6010 f"before rebuilding under current " 

6011 f"process_options" 

6012 ) 

6013 logger.info(log_message) 

6014 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

6015 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = log_message 

6016 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, log_message) 

6017 await self._purge_doc_chunks_and_kg( 

6018 doc_id, 

6019 stored_chunk_ids, 

6020 pipeline_status=pipeline_status, 

6021 pipeline_status_lock=pipeline_status_lock, 

6022 ) 

6023 # The status_doc carries chunks_list / chunks_count from the prior 

6024 # run; clear them so subsequent state-machine upserts don't write 

6025 # back stale IDs. 

6026 # 

6027 # Persist that reset together with retiring the purge journal, in one 

6028 # targeted write. In-memory-only was not enough: the 

6029 # stored chunks_list kept pointing at chunks this purge just deleted, 

6030 # so a crash here left the row advertising them. Retiring the journal 

6031 # in the SAME write is what keeps the two consistent — a surviving 

6032 # ``completed`` journal would later collide with the next purge's 

6033 # operation id. kg_write_state is deliberately left untouched: it is 

6034 # monotonic, and this run's own merge will advance it if it gets that 

6035 # far. 

6036 await self._clear_kg_purge_journal( 

6037 doc_id, 

6038 extra_fields={"chunks_list": [], "chunks_count": 0}, 

6039 ) 

6040 status_doc.chunks_list = [] 

6041 status_doc.chunks_count = 0 

6042 

6043 async def _mark_graph_mutation_started( 

6044 self, doc_id: str, status_doc: DocProcessingStatus | None = None 

6045 ) -> None: 

6046 """Advance ``kg_write_state`` past the point of no return. 

6047 

6048 Awaited by ``merge_nodes_and_edges`` in the single window where "this 

6049 document has never touched the graph" stops being true: after both 

6050 recovery anchors are flushed, before the first mutation. From here on a 

6051 purge may no longer assume there is nothing in the graph to find, so it 

6052 demands the anchors (or a purge journal) as proof. 

6053 

6054 Monotonic by construction — this is the only writer that sets 

6055 ``graph_mutation_started``, and no path writes ``pre_graph`` back. 

6056 Raising aborts the merge before any mutation, which is the safe 

6057 direction: the anchors are already durable. 

6058 

6059 ``status_doc`` is the caller's in-memory snapshot, and updating it is 

6060 NOT optional bookkeeping: every later transition upsert rebuilds 

6061 ``metadata`` from that object via ``doc_status_transition_metadata``, so 

6062 leaving it stale makes the PROCESSED write carry ``pre_graph`` forward 

6063 and silently revert this marker. A PROCESSED document would then claim 

6064 it never touched the graph — reinstating exactly the silent-skip the 

6065 marker exists to prevent. 

6066 

6067 Raises when the row cannot be read (strict where the backend supports 

6068 it), has vanished, or the update fails. The document is mid-merge 

6069 under the pipeline reservation, so the row is guaranteed to exist — 

6070 an unreadable row is the read failing, not the document being gone. 

6071 Returning silently instead would let the merge proceed with the 

6072 stored marker still ``pre_graph``: the graph gets written, and if the 

6073 anchors are later lost, that stale marker is a false proof licensing 

6074 a purge to skip graph cleanup — the exact defect fail-closed prevents. 

6075 """ 

6076 stored = await require_doc_status_record( 

6077 self.doc_status, doc_id, purpose="advance kg_write_state" 

6078 ) 

6079 raw_metadata = doc_status_field(stored, "metadata", {}) 

6080 metadata = dict(raw_metadata) if isinstance(raw_metadata, dict) else {} 

6081 metadata[KG_WRITE_STATE_METADATA_KEY] = KG_WRITE_STATE_GRAPH_MUTATION_STARTED 

6082 # missing_ok=False: the row vanishing between the read above and this 

6083 # write must abort the merge too, not silently skip the marker. 

6084 await self.doc_status.update_doc_status_fields(doc_id, {"metadata": metadata}) 

6085 await self._flush_storages([self.doc_status]) 

6086 if status_doc is not None: 6086 ↛ exitline 6086 didn't return from function '_mark_graph_mutation_started' because the condition on line 6086 was always true

6087 in_memory = getattr(status_doc, "metadata", None) 

6088 if isinstance(in_memory, dict): 6088 ↛ 6093line 6088 didn't jump to line 6093 because the condition on line 6088 was always true

6089 in_memory[KG_WRITE_STATE_METADATA_KEY] = ( 

6090 KG_WRITE_STATE_GRAPH_MUTATION_STARTED 

6091 ) 

6092 else: 

6093 status_doc.metadata = dict(metadata) 

6094 

6095 # ============================================================ 

6096 # doc_status state-machine helpers (shared by all layers) 

6097 # ============================================================ 

6098 

6099 async def _upsert_doc_status_transition( 

6100 self, 

6101 doc_id: str, 

6102 status: DocStatus, 

6103 status_doc: DocProcessingStatus, 

6104 file_path: str, 

6105 *, 

6106 ctx: "_BatchRunContext", 

6107 extra_fields: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

6108 metadata_extra: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

6109 metadata_drop: tuple[str, ...] = (), 

6110 ) -> None: 

6111 """Single source of truth for doc_status state-transition upserts. 

6112 

6113 Mirrors the field set used at every PARSING / ANALYZING / PROCESSING / 

6114 PROCESSED / FAILED transition. ``extra_fields`` carries 

6115 ``chunks_count`` / ``chunks_list`` / ``error_msg``; ``metadata_extra`` 

6116 is forwarded to ``doc_status_transition_metadata`` so carry-over 

6117 fields (e.g. ``process_options``) survive every state change. 

6118 ``metadata_drop`` is forwarded as its ``drop`` argument — the only way 

6119 to retire a carried-over metadata key at a transition. 

6120 

6121 Owner-checked (LR2 §7.7 items 3/4/7): every worker status write verifies 

6122 its run still owns ``busy`` immediately before writing, and a run whose 

6123 ownership was reclaimed DISCARDS the result with a warning instead of 

6124 writing. Without this, a storage/LLM response arriving late in a run that 

6125 was already declared dead could stamp a final status over the new owner's 

6126 work — including re-FAILING a document the manual exclusive reset had just 

6127 moved to PENDING, which would ACK the retry with the document still 

6128 failed. ``ctx`` is required so a new call site has to state which run the 

6129 write belongs to. 

6130 """ 

6131 if not await self._still_run_owner(ctx): 

6132 logger.warning( 

6133 f"[stale-writer] Discarded {getattr(status, 'value', status)} " 

6134 f"status write for {doc_id} ({file_path}): this run no longer " 

6135 f"owns the pipeline (ownership was reclaimed), so the result is " 

6136 f"late and must not overwrite the current owner's state" 

6137 ) 

6138 return 

6139 payload: dict[str, Any] = { 

6140 "status": status, 

6141 "content_summary": status_doc.content_summary, 

6142 "content_length": status_doc.content_length, 

6143 "created_at": status_doc.created_at, 

6144 "updated_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), 

6145 "file_path": file_path, 

6146 "track_id": status_doc.track_id, 

6147 "content_hash": status_doc.content_hash, 

6148 "metadata": doc_status_transition_metadata( 

6149 status_doc, extra=metadata_extra, drop=metadata_drop 

6150 ), 

6151 } 

6152 if extra_fields: 

6153 payload.update(extra_fields) 

6154 await self.doc_status.upsert({doc_id: payload}) 

6155 

6156 async def _raise_if_cancelled( 

6157 self, 

6158 pipeline_status: dict, 

6159 pipeline_status_lock, 

6160 ) -> None: 

6161 """Raise ``PipelineCancelledException`` if the user has requested cancel.""" 

6162 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

6163 if pipeline_status.get("cancellation_requested", False): 

6164 raise PipelineCancelledException("User cancelled") 

6165 

6166 @staticmethod 

6167 def _cancellation_label(pipeline_status: dict) -> str: 

6168 """Human-readable cancel cause: internal error (with detail) vs user. 

6169 

6170 Callers building cancellation messages use this so an internal abort 

6171 (e.g. a storage flush failure) is not mislabeled as a user cancel. 

6172 """ 

6173 if pipeline_status.get("cancellation_reason") == "internal_error": 

6174 detail = pipeline_status.get("cancellation_detail") or "unknown" 

6175 return f"Cancelled by internal error: {detail}" 

6176 return "User cancelled" 

6177 

6178 @staticmethod 

6179 def _internal_halt_message(label: str) -> str: 

6180 """Actionable halt message for an internal-error abort. 

6181 

6182 Shared by the loop-top cancellation handler and the finally cleanup so 

6183 the same wording surfaces whichever exit path the batch takes. 

6184 """ 

6185 return ( 

6186 f"Pipeline halted on internal storage error ({label}). Resolve the " 

6187 f"storage issue and restart processing; affected documents remain " 

6188 f"queued (PENDING/FAILED)." 

6189 ) 

6190 

6191 async def _cancellation_requested( 

6192 self, 

6193 pipeline_status: dict, 

6194 pipeline_status_lock, 

6195 ) -> bool: 

6196 """Read-only cancellation check. 

6197 

6198 Use this when a worker wants to branch on the flag (e.g. drain a queue 

6199 item) instead of raising. Callers that prefer the exception style 

6200 should use :meth:`_raise_if_cancelled` instead. 

6201 """ 

6202 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

6203 return bool(pipeline_status.get("cancellation_requested", False)) 

6204 

6205 async def _persist_chunk_cache_references_best_effort( 

6206 self, 

6207 *, 

6208 stage_label: str, 

6209 doc_id: str, 

6210 error: BaseException | None = None, 

6211 ) -> bool: 

6212 """Commit the chunk rows carrying this document's cache references. 

6213 

6214 Returns False when the commit did not land — the caller's signal NOT to 

6215 commit the LLM cache afterwards. Pass the exception that triggered the 

6216 epilogue as ``error``: a flush this epilogue cannot redo is reported 

6217 through it, not through the retry below. See *LLM extraction cache 

6218 reachability* in the contract doc, 

6219 ``docs/design/PurgeRecoveryContract.md``. 

6220 

6221 Runs for every stage epilogue, not just the extract one that can hold 

6222 chunk references. At the parse stage there is nothing of this 

6223 document's to commit, so the cost is one no-op flush; suppressing the 

6224 cache commit there can only happen when ``text_chunks`` is already 

6225 failing, and it costs a recomputable cache entry. Both are cheaper than 

6226 a stage whitelist that has to stay correct as stages move. 

6227 """ 

6228 if self.text_chunks is None: 6228 ↛ 6229line 6228 didn't jump to line 6229 because the condition on line 6228 was never true

6229 return True 

6230 # A retry cannot see a failure the backend already discarded. When the 

6231 # aborting flush was text_chunks' own, a per-item backend has dropped 

6232 # the permanently-failed operation from its buffer before raising

7882 f"unexpected error: {texc}" 

7883 ) 

7884 

7885 try: 

7886 sidecar_path.write_text( 

7887 json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), 

7888 encoding="utf-8", 

7889 ) 

7890 except OSError as exc: 

7891 logger.warning( 

7892 f"[analyze_multimodal] failed to write sidecar " 

7893 f"{sidecar_path}: {exc}" 

7894 ) 

7895 

7896 if fail_fast_exc is not None: 

7897 # Best-effort cache flush so any cache_ids written by 

7898 # already-completed sibling tasks survive a restart — 

7899 # otherwise the sidecar references cache rows that 

7900 # haven't been persisted yet. Mirrors 

7901 # _finalize_doc_failure's PROCESS-stage behaviour. 

7902 await self._persist_llm_response_cache_best_effort( 

7903 stage_label="multimodal analyze fail-fast", 

7904 doc_id=doc_id, 

7905 ) 

7906 raise fail_fast_exc 

7907 

7908 # Successful multimodal cache rows used to wait until the much 

7909 # later PROCESS-stage _insert_done. Commit after the analysis 

7910 # sidecar has been written so a restart can reuse the result as 

7911 # soon as this stage has completed. 

7912 await self._persist_llm_response_cache_best_effort( 

7913 stage_label="multimodal analyze", 

7914 doc_id=doc_id, 

7915 ) 

7916 if mm_truncation_tally: 

7917 truncation_message = ( 

7918 f"Warning: token-limit truncation hit " 

7919 f"{mm_truncation_tally.affected} multimodal analyses for " 

7920 f"{file_path} ({mm_truncation_tally.events} responses); " 

7921 f"descriptions may be incomplete" 

7922 ) 

7923 logger.warning(truncation_message) 

7924 if pipeline_status is not None and pipeline_status_lock is not None: 7924 ↛ 7925line 7924 didn't jump to line 7925 because the condition on line 7924 was never true

7925 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

7926 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = truncation_message 

7927 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, truncation_message) 

7928 parsed_data["multimodal_processed"] = True 

7929 logger.info(f"[analyze_multimodal] completed for d-id: {doc_id}") 

7930 except PipelineCancelledException: 

7931 # Must re-raise BEFORE the generic Exception handler below, 

7932 # otherwise the doc would be returned as if analyze succeeded 

7933 # and would advance to PROCESS instead of being marked FAILED. 

7934 raise 

7935 except MultimodalAnalysisError: 

7936 raise 

7937 except Exception as e: 

7938 logger.warning(f"[analyze_multimodal] failed for d-id: {doc_id}: {e}") 

7939 finally: 

7940 # Analyze→process hand-off of the truncation record, on EVERY 

7941 # exit — not just success. Ride the hand-off dict rather than 

7942 # doc_status: LLM_TRUNCATION_METADATA_KEY is per-attempt (not 

7943 # carried over), so a stamp written here would be dropped at the 

7944 # PROCESSING transition. Consumers: on success and on the 

7945 # soft-swallowed exits the process stage merges it into its own 

7946 # tally at the terminal write; when this call raises (a sibling 

7947 # item's fail-fast failure, mid-VLM cancellation), the analyze 

7948 # worker stamps it onto the FAILED row. A success-only hand-off 

7949 # lost an accepted truncated analysis on exactly those raising 

7950 # exits — the item's partial result was already written to the 

7951 # sidecar, but the document's metadata never learned of it. 

7952 if mm_truncation_tally: 

7953 parsed_data["llm_truncation"] = mm_truncation_tally.as_metadata() 

7954 return parsed_data

7956 def _build_mm_chunks_from_sidecars( 

7957 self, 

7958 doc_id: str, 

7959 file_path: str, 

7960 blocks_path: str, 

7961 base_order_index: int, 

7962 process_options: str | None = None, 

7963 ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: 

7964 """Build multimodal chunks from sidecars carrying analysis results. 

7965 

7966 Only items whose ``llm_analyze_result.status == "success"`` produce 

7967 chunks. ``"skipped"`` items are silently ignored; ``"failure"`` 

7968 items raise :class:`MultimodalAnalysisError` so the document is 

7969 marked failed (a failure should already have aborted the analyze 

7970 phase — this is a defensive recheck). 

7971 

7972 Each chunk follows the new schema: nested ``heading`` and 

7973 ``sidecar`` dicts, no flat ``parent_headings`` / ``level`` / 

7974 ``content_type`` fields. ``llm_cache_list`` is merged from the 

7975 underlying sidecar item so document deletion can clean up the 

7976 ``cache_type="analysis"`` entries it created. 

7977 

7978 ``process_options`` gates which modality sidecars are read: a 

7979 document re-processed after opting out of ``i`` / ``t`` / ``e`` 

7980 must NOT pick up stale success results from a prior pass. When 

7981 ``None`` (e.g. ad-hoc unit tests), every modality is considered. 

7982 

7983 Raises: 

7984 MultimodalAnalysisError: when an item carries ``status="failure"``, 

7985 or when the multimodal chunk cannot be fit under the 

7986 extraction token budget even after truncating description 

7987 to :data:`DEFAULT_MM_CHUNK_DESCRIPTION_MIN_TOKENS`. 

7988 """ 

7989 from lightrag.constants import ( 

7990 DEFAULT_MAX_EXTRACT_INPUT_TOKENS, 

7991 DEFAULT_MM_CHUNK_DESCRIPTION_MIN_TOKENS, 

7992 ) 

7993 from lightrag.parser.routing import parse_process_options 

7994 

7995 block_file = Path(blocks_path) 

7996 if not block_file.exists(): 

7997 return [] 

7998 

7999 base = str(block_file) 

8000 if base.endswith(".blocks.jsonl"): 8000 ↛ 8003line 8000 didn't jump to line 8003 because the condition on line 8000 was always true

8001 base = base[: -len(".blocks.jsonl")] 

8002 

8003 if process_options is None: 

8004 allowed = {"drawing", "table", "equation"} 

8005 else: 

8006 opts = parse_process_options(process_options) 

8007 allowed = set() 

8008 if opts.images: 

8009 allowed.add("drawing") 

8010 if opts.tables: 

8011 allowed.add("table") 

8012 if opts.equations: 

8013 allowed.add("equation") 

8014 

8015 sidecar_defs = [ 

8016 (root, Path(base + suffix), kind) 

8017 for root, suffix, kind in ( 

8018 ("drawings", ".drawings.json", "drawing"), 

8019 ("tables", ".tables.json", "table"), 

8020 ("equations", ".equations.json", "equation"), 

8021 ) 

8022 if kind in allowed 

8023 ]

8025 mm_chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

8029 if v is None: 

8030 return [] 

8031 if isinstance(v, list): 8031 ↛ 8034line 8031 didn't jump to line 8034 because the condition on line 8031 was always true

8032 cleaned = (sanitize_text_for_encoding(str(x)) for x in v) 

8033 return [s for s in cleaned if s] 

8034 s = sanitize_text_for_encoding(str(v)) 

8035 return [s] if s else []

8038 if not isinstance(value, list): 

8039 return [] 

8040 cleaned = (sanitize_text_for_encoding(str(p or "")) for p in value) 

8041 return [p for p in cleaned if p]

8043 def _build_heading_dict(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None: 

8044 heading_raw = item.get("heading") 

8045 if isinstance(heading_raw, dict): 

8046 heading_text = sanitize_text_for_encoding( 

8047 str(heading_raw.get("heading") or "") 

8048 )

8052 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

8053 level = 0 

8054 else: 

8055 heading_text = sanitize_text_for_encoding(str(heading_raw or "")) 

8056 parents = _norm_parent_headings(item.get("parent_headings")) 

8057 try: 

8058 level = int(item.get("level") or 0) 

8059 except (TypeError, ValueError):

8061 if not heading_text and not parents and level == 0:

8063 return {

8065 "heading": heading_text,

8069 def _render( 

8070 kind: str,

8078 # leading labels below are a contract consumed by

8080 # ``_MM_DISPLAY_NAME_PATTERN``). If you rename or restructure 

8081 # these labels, update that regex too, or relation descriptions 

8082 # will silently fall back to sidecar ids. The 

8083 # ``test_parse_mm_display_name_on_real_builder_output`` 

8084 # regression pins this contract end-to-end.

8086 head = f"[Image Name]{name}\n[Image Type]{image_type}" 

8087 footnote_label = "Image Footnotes" 

8088 elif kind == "table":

8105 continue
